directions.question: When a decentralized organizational team realizes a complex adaptive system, how does reorganization of local interaction patterns regain workable alignment after coordination impairment?

logical_move.G_S: Complex adaptive systems of interacting adaptive agents
logical_move.relation: Conditional realization of a broader dynamical system class, rather than substitution of another kind of team. Distributed authority alone does not establish adaptive dynamics.
logical_move.membership_justification: Represent members/units as agents, their interdependent exchanges as interactions, and changes in action rules as adaptation; the representation requires observed local adaptation and system-level emergent patterns.
invariants: Local agency and adaptation under changing conditions
non_coercive_conditions: Members can adjust coordination through consent and local discretion
Interaction evidence comes from work processes or voluntary reports rather than employee surveillance

directions.discovery_target: Whether altered interaction connectivity and enabling conditions, rather than replacement of a single leader, precede recovery of interdependent task alignment.

queries: Uhl-Bien Marion McKelvey 2007 complexity leadership theory organizations complex adaptive systems pdf

directions.bridge_test: First show that an actual team has distributed decision rights plus adaptive interacting agents; document impaired task alignment, changes in local interaction patterns, and subsequent workable alignment. Compare recovery and failed recovery while separating coordination outcomes from innovation or generic adaptability. Reject the bridge if adaptation occurs without regained coordination.
directions.novelty_reason: Introduces emergence, interaction topology and adaptive dynamics as measurable system properties; it is not a new label for decentralization.
unknowns: Whether all or which anchor teams satisfy CAS criteria
Whether the retrieved adaptive capacity framework predicts recovery rather than innovation
Decision-right distribution and non-coercion in the retrieved emergency-team study are unverified
Recovery threshold and counterfactual remain unspecified

fixed.S: Organizational teams with decision authority distributed among members or units; membership of any broader theoretical class remains to be tested.
fixed.P: Regain a workable capacity to align interdependent activity after impairment; earlier or different workable arrangement allowed.
fixed.C: After a disruption, with onset/end, duration and severity unspecified; temporal order alone does not establish causation.
fixed.scope: Non-coercive organizational coordination; exclude employee surveillance and military command.

changed.predicate: P is retained; adaptation is a candidate explanatory variable, not a replacement outcome

directions.finding: The primary article abstract frames organizational leadership through interactions from which adaptive outcomes emerge. A separate primary search result describes emergency medical teams and temporal coordination restructuring. These support a theoretical framing and an adjacent empirical route, respectively; neither establishes recovery transfer to non-coercive teams with distributed authority.

candidate_validity.reason: The CAS class is broader than organizational teams, but adaptive interaction is an additional membership requirement absent from the anchor. A universal lift would be unsupported.

directions.question: For a decentralized team that instantiates a polycentric institutional system, can coordination recovery after impairment be explained by renegotiating interfaces among autonomous decision centers?

logical_move.G_S: Polycentric institutional systems with mutually adjusting decision centers
logical_move.relation: Conditional institutional representation spanning collectives at multiple scales, not replacement by another team sector.
logical_move.membership_justification: Members or units must have actual autonomous decision jurisdictions, recognize interdependence, and sustain workable inter-center arrangements. Mere delegation or multiple physical locations is insufficient.
invariants: Rules or workable interfaces for mutual adjustment
non_coercive_conditions: Use voluntary horizontal coordination and participants able to negotiate arrangements
Inspect civil-society cooperation separately from compulsory or militarized crisis structures
Do not import punitive enforcement or member monitoring as a recovery recommendation

directions.discovery_target: How recognition of autonomous participants, interface agreements and voluntarily assigned coordinating roles affect recovery.

queries: Ostrom 2010 beyond markets and states polycentric governance complex economic systems pdf

directions.bridge_test: Map actual team decision jurisdictions to distinct centers and specify how they can negotiate without compulsion. Trace a pre-impairment arrangement, actual breakdown, interface changes, and restored alignment. Civil-society crisis response demonstrates only a possible mechanism unless the same temporal impairment/recovery sequence is measured. Test whether class membership fails for teams with no institutionalized centers.
directions.novelty_reason: Moves from a bounded team to an institutional configuration of autonomous centers; predicts interface and legitimacy problems that a team label does not specify.
unknowns: Shared-rule requirements remain theoretically contested
Whether an individual team has distinct centers rather than merely delegated tasks
The retrieved volunteer episode does not report a recovery baseline or threshold
Mixed crisis-management contexts contain out-of-scope command relations; no transfer from those relations is claimed

fixed.S: Organizational teams with decision authority distributed among members or units; membership of any broader theoretical class remains to be tested.
fixed.P: Regain a workable capacity to align interdependent activity after impairment; earlier or different workable arrangement allowed.
fixed.C: After a disruption, with onset/end, duration and severity unspecified; temporal order alone does not establish causation.
fixed.scope: Non-coercive organizational coordination; exclude employee surveillance and military command.

changed.predicate: Coordination recovery remains P; crisis response performance alone is insufficient

directions.finding: A primary crisis-governance article defines polycentricity through autonomous, interdependent units. A separate primary civil-society study reports an emergent volunteer organization using shared rosters, task division and an assigned coordinator when coordination became difficult. Only the non-command volunteer episode is relevant here; the source also contains excluded command practices. This is a concrete candidate bridge, not established team recovery.

candidate_validity.reason: Distinct autonomous decision centers are a plausible institutional representation of some anchor teams, but distributed authority alone does not prove those centers or their interfaces exist.
candidate_validity.recovery_transfer: not established; candidate episode lacks baseline and authority audit

directions.question: If a decentralized team and its shared work artifacts realize a distributed cognitive system, how does reestablishing propagation of task-relevant representations restore coordination after impairment?

logical_move.G_S: Distributed cognitive systems spanning people, artifacts and work practice
logical_move.relation: Explicit realization/representation relation; the team alone is not literally identical to the people-plus-artifacts system.
logical_move.membership_justification: The joint task must depend on transformations or propagation of information across members and material/digital representations. The system boundary is enlarged transparently to include artifacts actually used in the team task.
invariants: Cross-component dependencies necessary for joint task performance
non_coercive_conditions: Use shared task artifacts with participant consent
No personal tracking or employee-surveillance systems
Retain distributed decision authority; informational centrality is not decision centrality

directions.discovery_target: Whether repair of shared representations, handoffs and artifact availability explains recovery independently of formal reporting lines.

queries: Hutchins distributed cognition cognitive system people artifacts organization pdf
Hollan Hutchins Kirsh 2000 distributed cognition human computer interaction dynamic configure subsystems coordination pdf author

directions.bridge_test: Locate a specific impaired interdependent task; trace which shared representation or handoff failed, what actors/artifacts repaired it, and whether task alignment recovered. Hold the people/artifact boundary constant over time. Verify decision authority separately, because successful distributed cognition can coexist with centralized authority.
directions.novelty_reason: Adds representational media and propagation paths as elements of the subject; distinguishes cognitive distribution from distribution of authority.
unknowns: Whether the anchor task is appropriately modeled as cognitive work
Whether the manufacturing case had distributed decision rights or non-coercive coordination
The control-room-centered case is not evidence that authority was decentralized
No causal estimate of artifact repair on recovery was retrieved

changed.subject_level: Team → realized cognitive system including relevant artifacts
changed.predicate: P retained; representational propagation is a proposed mechanism

directions.finding: The primary author-hosted abstract explicitly focuses on interactions among people and technologies and coordination in whole work environments. A primary manufacturing-study search excerpt reports cognitive artifacts mediating interruption handling. The latter also mentions control-room-centered communication, so its success cannot establish transfer to decentralized authority. The representation is plausible; recovery remains to be tested.

candidate_validity.reason: A broader theoretical object can represent some teams, but it requires a task-specific cognition/artifact mapping; it is not a strict set-inclusion assertion for every team.

directions.question: When a decentralized team is modeled as a sociotechnical work system, does restoring the fit between social decision arrangements and technical task dependencies recover coordination after impairment?

logical_move.G_S: Sociotechnical work systems with coupled social and technical subsystems
logical_move.relation: Conditional work-system representation, broader than teams because it also covers organizational systems with many units and technologies.
logical_move.membership_justification: Specify an actual work task and its technical/material/procedural constraints alongside member roles and distributed decision rights. Their coupling, not mere co-presence of humans and tools, warrants the model.
invariants: Local choices affect system-level task performance
non_coercive_conditions: Participants can shape work design and renegotiate roles
Use work-relevant feedback rather than employee surveillance
Do not equate self-regulation or a managerial design label with consent

directions.discovery_target: Whether repair should target coupled work design and resource/authority mismatches rather than communication volume alone.

queries: sociotechnical systems theory organizational work systems self regulating groups joint optimization Cherns 1976 abstract

directions.bridge_test: Before applying the model, map technical task dependencies and who has authority/resources to alter them. Observe an impairment that creates a mismatch, a participatory repair, and subsequent alignment. Model-based network recovery is not sufficient evidence: reject transfer if the model only restores infrastructure service or assumes away consent, power or team cognition.
directions.novelty_reason: Changes the analytic unit to a coupled work system and introduces joint design constraints, distinguishing it from a cognition-only representation.
unknowns: The original anchor does not specify a technical subsystem
The retrieved recovery model was not opened and its assumptions and outcome measures remain unverified
A participative design principle does not establish post-impairment recovery efficacy
How to operationalize non-coercion in resource/authority changes

fixed.P: Regain a workable capacity to align interdependent activity after impairment; earlier or different workable arrangement allowed.
fixed.C: After a disruption, with onset/end, duration and severity unspecified; temporal order alone does not establish causation.
fixed.scope: Non-coercive organizational coordination; exclude employee surveillance and military command.

directions.finding: Cummings’s primary abstract locates self-regulating work groups in sociotechnical systems theory, providing a direct organizational class bridge. A separate primary paper’s search excerpt describes a decentralized recovery model with heterogeneous agents and bottom-up dynamics. That model is a lead, not verified evidence of team coordination recovery. Cherns’s primary full text could not be read in the returned PDF text.

candidate_validity.reason: A genuinely broader work-system structure is available, but task coupling and non-coercive design conditions must be established for an actual anchor team.

directions.question: For those decentralized teams that qualify as group agents, does repair of collectively coherent judgments and goals explain coordination recovery after impairment?

logical_move.G_S: Group agents with collective representational and goal-seeking states
logical_move.relation: Attempted conditional inclusion in an agent-theoretic class; rejected as an unconditional superordinate of S.
logical_move.membership_justification: A team must sustain collective beliefs/goals, revise them coherently, and act on them through its members. None follows merely from distributed decision authority. Many coordinated teams may lack a single group-level agent.
invariants: A mechanism linking member contributions to collective action
non_coercive_conditions: Members authorize and can contest collective decision procedures
No spokesperson or majority procedure is treated as evidence of consent by itself
No coercive enforcement or employee surveillance is inferred from group rationality

directions.discovery_target: Whether collective judgment inconsistency can produce misaligned actions and whether authorized revision repairs that particular failure.

queries: Christian List Philip Pettit group agency organizational groups agent rationality institutional pdf

directions.bridge_test: Establish independent behavioral evidence of group-level judgments/goals before testing recovery. Compare a judgment-inconsistency impairment with coordination impairments caused by missing resources or incompatible tasks. Test whether deliberative revision restores the specified alignment; reject the lift if collective agency is merely attributed from team membership.
directions.novelty_reason: Introduces requirements for collective agency and judgment aggregation, distinct from interaction dynamics, institutional centers, information propagation and sociotechnical fit.
unknowns: Anchor supplies no collective rationality or group-state evidence
No pertinent primary recovery study was returned by the targeted query
The opened author PDF had no text lines available
Group coherence need not be necessary or sufficient for coordination

fixed.P: Regain a workable capacity to align interdependent activity after impairment; earlier or different workable arrangement allowed.
fixed.C: After a disruption, with onset/end, duration and severity unspecified; temporal order alone does not establish causation.
fixed.scope: Non-coercive organizational coordination; exclude employee surveillance and military command.

changed.predicate: Coordination recovery retained; collective rationality is a possible explanatory property, not a replacement for P

directions.finding: The primary author-paper search excerpt specifies representational and goal-seeking states with rationality conditions, while the publisher’s introduction presents group agency as a substantive theoretical position. This establishes a distinct theoretical object, but supplies neither membership evidence for the anchor teams nor a recovery mechanism. The proposed unconditional lift fails; the question remains a conditional hypothesis for a restricted subset.

candidate_validity.reason: Group agents are not shown to contain all decentralized teams. Claiming S ⊆ G_S would silently add substantive agency and rationality conditions; the anchor does not license them.
